meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: not later than the working day following discharge
facts.summary: District of Columbia: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the working day following discharge.
facts.evidence_quote: (1) Whenever an employer discharges an employee, the employer shall pay the employee's wages earned not later than the working day following such discharge
facts.source_title: D.C. Code 32-1303, Payment of wages upon discharge or resignation
facts.source_publisher: Council of the District of Columbia (D.C. Law Library)
facts.notes: 4-day allowance where the employee is responsible for employer monies (same subsection).

facts.value: next regular payday or within 7 days of quitting, whichever is earlier
facts.summary: District of Columbia: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday or within 7 days of quitting, whichever is earlier.
facts.evidence_quote: (2) Whenever an employee (not having a written contract of employment for a period in excess of 30 days) quits or resigns, the employer shall pay the employee's wages due upon the next regular payday or within 7 days from the date of quitting or resigning, whichever is earlier.
facts.source_title: D.C. Code 32-1303, Payment of wages upon discharge or resignation
facts.source_publisher: Council of the District of Columbia (D.C. Law Library)

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: District of Columbia basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $18.40.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $18.40 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 The minimum wage is adjusted annually on July 1 based on a set formula.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: Within 20 days of hire (or rehire) date
facts.summary: District of Columbia new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire (or rehire) date

facts.summary: District of Columbia is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
